title: Introduce soft-spike attenuator with delayed-provision lockstep and utilization fence
author: Priya Nandakumar
description: Context: Customers operating Dedicated fleets observe transient demand spikes that trigger immediate provisioning which increases cost and creates oscillation risk. This PR implements a soft-spike attenuation layer that defers aggressive provisioning for short-living microbursts and pairs it with a delayed-provision lockstep path for verified sustained demand. The change also introduces a lightweight utilization-fence telemetry signal to improve signal fidelity for autoscalers. What this does: 1) soft-spike-attenuator: transient spikes under a configurable time window (default 9s) are met with a graded throttle that prefers pre-warmed warmlets and soft-burst credits rather than immediate fleet-wide capacity changes; 2) delayed-provision-lockstep: when the attenuator detects sustained demand beyond the configured hysteresis and confidence threshold, it releases a coordinated provision pulse to fleet manager which performs staged instance onboarding (lockstep) to avoid overshoot; 3) utilization-fence: an aggregated, locally-windowed utilization metric emitted per pool that discounts prefix-KV cached tokens and synthetic probe traffic to reduce noise in autoscaler decisions. Includes feature-flag gating and observability. Design notes: heuristics chosen to favor availability for latency-sensitive tenants while reducing unnecessary scaling churn and cost. Rollback: feature flag off at gate, immediate revert path to remove attestation checkpoints. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for attenuator decision logic - [x] Integration tests with fleet-manager simulator - [x] End-to-end canary (10% pools) - [x] Telemetry dashboard and alerting rules - [x] Documentation and API config schema Changes: See changed_files. Impact: Expected to reduce short-term provisioning actions by ~48% in microburst workloads based on replayed traces. Requires minimal operator tuning (two knobs: spike_window_seconds, confidence_threshold).

ci_summary: Checks: unit-tests passed (88s), integration-sim passed (230s), e2e-canary initially failed on timing (flaky) then rerun and passed, lint passed, build passed. Codecov delta +0.6%. Canary pipeline required one rerun due to environment timing; no regressions in perf smoke tests.
release_notes: Introduce soft-spike attenuator and delayed-provision lockstep to reduce unnecessary capacity churn on Dedicated fleets. New operator knobs: spike_window_seconds (default 9s), confidence_threshold (default 0.75), staged_lockstep_step_size. Backwards compatible; disabled by default behind feature flag `soft_spike_attenuator`. Recommended canary: 10% pools for 48h.
rationale: Observed overshoot and oscillation when autoscalers treat short microbursts as sustained demand. By deferring provisioning for very short spikes and relying on existing warmlet capacity and soft credits, we reduce cost and churn while preserving latency SLOs. The utilization-fence improves signal quality for the autoscaler and reduces false positives from probe or cached traffic.
tests: Unit tests cover decision boundaries for spike windows, confidence scoring, and cache-tagged samples. Integration tests run against the fleet-manager simulator with synthetic spike and sustained patterns. Canary workload: replay of 3 customer traces with 48h window showed 45-52% fewer provision events and <2% change in 99th latency for latency-sensitive tenants. Load tests included memory/regression profiling to ensure no allocator leaks.
rollout_plan: Gate behind feature flag. Stage 0: internal canary on non-prod fleets (2 pools) 3h. Stage 1: 10% production pools for 48h with histogram monitors for provision events and tail latency. Stage 2: 50% for 72h with ops on-call watch. Full rollout if metrics stable and no SLO regressions. Quick rollback: flip flag off and drain attenuator queues; revert PR if issues.
risk_mitigation: Feature flag and small default window minimize blast radius. Staged lockstep reduces overshoot risk. Added alerting for 'provision delay' and 'attenuator backpressure' to alert SRE if attenuator defers too long. Clear operator runbook included.
notes: Operator playbook included under examples/canary/playbook.md. Config schema added to services/autoscaler/config.yaml.schema. This PR coordinates with ENG-1249 (autoscaler signal hygiene) and ENG-1398 (fleet-manager staged provisioning).
